content:
A common misconception of HR in the Hong Kong Banking industry with regards to registration under the SFO/hiring of securities professionals is that they think:

People who are registered as Licensed Representatives/Responsible Officers in investment firms are not qualified to become Executive Officers/Relevant Individuals in banks.

That is WRONG.

In fact they are the exact equivalent, with the same criteria and supervision responsibilities (Executive Officer). While there are some differences in terms of how they regulate the business, a Responsible Officer of an investment firm, whether it be a brokerage, fund manager, or a private equity principal, will be fully qualified to be an Executive Officer in terms of overseeing the business in bank operated brokerage, compliance, etc.

I had registration as an Relevant Individual under the HKMA previously, and majority of my career as a Responsible Officer of many investment firms. Therefore, there is no reason why Banks cannot hire investment professionals or vice versa.

Hope this clarification will be relevant and make hiring much more smoother, with a much bigger pool for potential employers and ex-banking/investment/brokerage employees to choose from.
